# Architecture

For a reader deciding whether to trust the decisions this system records.

On the frozen corpus the flow reduces to: **2,000 webhook events &rarr; 1,611 normalized customers (369 with more than one failure) &rarr; 1,611 recorded decisions** (`process_failure` is idempotent per `payment_id`), of which **1,126 reached ACT** and walked the guardrail ladder, writing **7,882 `guardrail_evaluations` rows** (7 per rung attempted, never collapsed). Arm assignment splits those 1,611 customers 1,126 treatment / 485 control. The whole path is exercised by **271 tests** (`pytest -q`).
<!-- END GENERATED NUMBERS -->

## Data flow: webhook → decision → audit

```
 Razorpay                      app/  (the pipeline — sees no ground truth)
 ────────                      ─────────────────────────────────────────────
 POST /webhooks/razorpay
      │
      ▼
 verify_signature ............ HMAC_SHA256(secret, raw_bytes); mismatch → 401, nothing stored
      │
      ▼
 store_raw_event ............. INSERT raw body+headers BEFORE any parse; event_id UNIQUE (redelivery = no-op)
      │
      ▼
 json.loads .................. malformed → 400, raw row already saved, process stays up
      │
      ▼
 events / audit .............. payment-keyed state + append-only trail  ┐
      │                                                                 │  Slice 2
      ▼                                                                 │
 (payment settled failed)                                              ─┘
      │
      ▼
 ingest_live_failure ......... Slice 4 card_failure adapter → one normalized_events row
      │                        (customer_id, email, phone, amount_paise, occurred_at, reference)
      ▼
 diagnose(row) ............... Slice 6 rules: error_code → cause  (RULES_CONFIDENCE = 0.32, flat)
      │                        └─ ambiguous BAD_REQUEST_ERROR only ─► app/llm_diagnosis.py
      │                                                              (advisory; TAIL_ACT_ENABLED=False
      │                                                               → recorded + routed to a human,
      │                                                               never spends)
      ▼
 assign_arm(seed, customer_id)  Slice 5: sha256("assign:{seed}:{customer_id}") → treatment | control
      │
      ▼
 decide(event, policy, arm, history)  Slice 7 pure function:
      │   a) hard gates      RISK_BLOCKED, ALREADY_RECOVERED, NO_CONTACT_CHANNEL, COOLDOWN, PRIOR_ZERO
      │   b) EV per rung     p_effective·effectiveness (cap .95)·ticket − cost, best rung wins
      │   c) control arm     → SKIP CONTROL_ARM (records the shadow rung it *would* have fired)
      │   d) EV < floor      → SKIP EV_BELOW_FLOOR
      │   e) policy override → ROUTE_TO_HUMAN  (agent_call rung, big ticket, weak diagnosis)
      │   f) else            → ACT with the best rung
      ▼
 walk_ladder + guardrails ... Slice 9, ACT only: 7 predicates per rung, evaluate-all-then-decide,
      │                        best-first; all blocked → BLOCKED/<first blocker>
      ▼
 record_decision ............ one flat row in `decisions` + one `audit` row, SAME transaction
      │                        (append-only: BEFORE UPDATE / BEFORE DELETE triggers RAISE(ABORT))
      │
      ▼
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │  app/dashboard/  — read-only, connect_ro("file:…?mode=ro")               │
 │  /metrics  /decisions  /trace/{id}  /not-chased  /queue                  │
 │  never imports eval/, never reads ground_truth, cannot write             │
 └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Why `datagen.py` and `eval/` are separated from `app/`

`datagen.py` writes the corpus; `eval/environment.py` decides whether a
customer recovers. **Nothing under `app/` imports either** — `grep -rn
"ground_truth\|from eval\|import eval" app/` is empty, and there is a test that
keeps it empty.

The reason is not tidiness. If the decision pipeline could read
`data/ground_truth.json`, it would be marking its own homework: it would know
each customer's true `p_would_pay_anyway` and `p_pay_if_nudged` and could
trivially "predict" recoveries. Keeping the latent parameters on the far side of
a wall the pipeline cannot reach is what makes the uplift measurement
meaningful — the pipeline decides from `error_code`, ticket size and contact
channel alone, exactly what it would have in production.

## Why arm assignment keys on `customer_id`, not `event_id`

`assign_arm(run_seed, customer_id)` is a pure `sha256("assign:{run_seed}:{customer_id}")`
draw — deterministic, order-independent, no DB. It keys on the **customer**, so
one customer stays in one arm across every repeat failure. Keyed on `event_id`,
a customer with three failures could land treatment / control / treatment; their
own later recoveries would then leak across the arm boundary and contaminate the
control baseline — the one number the whole experiment depends on. The hash is
also in its own `"assign:"` namespace, deliberately distinct from the
outcome-resolution draw (`sha256("{seed}:{customer_id}")`), so a customer's arm
is not correlated with whether they self-recover.

## Why the audit tables are append-only, enforced by SQLite triggers

`audit`, `decisions` and `guardrail_evaluations` each carry `BEFORE UPDATE` and
`BEFORE DELETE` triggers that `RAISE(ABORT, …)`. Any `UPDATE` or `DELETE` — from
application code, a bug, or a raw `sqlite3` console — fails at the database
level, regardless of who issues it.

What that buys: the `/trace/{id}` page can state, and mean, that a decision
record *cannot have been edited after the payment's outcome was known*. The
guarantee is a property of the file, not a promise about the code. A reviewer
does not have to audit every write path in `app/` to believe it.

## Why the dashboard opens the database read-only

Every SQLite handle in `app/dashboard/` is opened as
`sqlite3.connect("file:<path>?mode=ro", uri=True)` (`app.dashboard.live.connect_ro`,
the only opener in the package). A write attempt raises
`sqlite3.OperationalError` — there is a test that fires an `INSERT` through a
dashboard connection and asserts it raises. The dashboard *physically cannot*
mutate the decision record it displays, so "read-only view" is enforced, not
asserted. The served database is chosen by `DASHBOARD_DB_PATH`
(`app.dashboard.served`); when it is anything other than the live webhook DB,
every page carries a non-dismissible "corpus run — outcomes are simulated"
banner.

## Where the LLM path sits, and why it cannot spend

`app/llm_diagnosis.py` is an advisory classifier for the single failure cell the
rules layer cannot split (`BAD_REQUEST_ERROR`, a four-way collision). It is
called only when `is_ambiguous(entity)` is true; every other event keeps its
rules label.

`TAIL_ACT_ENABLED = False` is a hard gate: while it is false, any `Diagnosis`
whose source is `llm` or `llm_failed` is forced to the human queue *before* the
decision engine can authorise a paid action. It is barred because in the
synthetic corpus every failure's `error_description` is a fixed 1:1
transcription of its `error_reason` — a classifier that reads the description
scores a fake 1.00 by transcription. Until the tail is validated on data with
real description variation, an LLM-sourced diagnosis is recorded, queued for a
person, and never spends money. The rules path is unaffected.

## Component map

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `app/main.py` | FastAPI app: the webhook endpoint + the dashboard routers |
| `app/security.py` | HMAC signature verification |
| `app/db.py` | `events` / `audit` schema + append-only triggers |
| `app/ingest.py` | three upstream shapes → one `normalized_events` row |
| `app/diagnosis.py` | rules: `error_code` → root cause |
| `app/llm_diagnosis.py` | advisory LLM tail, barred from money actions |
| `app/arms.py` | deterministic treatment/control assignment |
| `app/decision/engine.py` | the pure decision function + EV ladder |
| `app/decision/store.py` | append-only `decisions` persistence |
| `app/guardrails.py` | the seven guardrails + the ladder walk |
| `app/pipeline.py` | wiring: ingest → diagnose → arm → decide → guardrails → record |
| `app/dashboard/` | the five read-only screens |
| `datagen.py`, `eval/` | corpus generation + outcome resolution — **outside `app/`** |
| `scripts/run_corpus.py` | the whole pipeline over the frozen 2,000-event corpus |
| `scripts/make_demo_db.py` | that run, persisted to `data/demo.db` for the dashboard |

See [`DECISIONS.md`](DECISIONS.md) for the rationale behind each choice, slice by
slice.
